message: This UPDATE rewrites every row of "holidays", in one statement.
why: A whole-table UPDATE locks every row it changes until the migration commits, so writes to those rows wait, and it writes a new version of each row. On a large table that takes long and leaves the table bloated until VACUUM.
safeAlternative: Check that the change is intended, and whether down() needs to restore the old values. On a large table, update in batches, for example by ranges of the primary key, outside the migration's transaction.

message: Adding check constraint "CHK_end" on "holidays" checks every row while blocking reads and writes to "holidays".
why: Adding a CHECK constraint scans the whole table to validate the existing rows, and holds an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock until the scan finishes.
safeAlternative: Add the constraint with NOT VALID, which applies it to new and changed rows without a scan. Then run ALTER TABLE ... VALIDATE CONSTRAINT in its own transaction, after the NOT VALID one has committed; it holds only a SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE lock, which does not block reads or writes. With TypeORM, migrationsTransactionMode "all" (the default) runs every pending migration in one transaction, so deploy the VALIDATE migration in a later release, or use "each". TypeORM builder calls cannot add NOT VALID, so use queryRunner.query().
